tools.name: get_signals
tools.description: Today's demand patterns from DECA's radar: groups of apps climbing the App Store and Google Play charts, with what people say and want about them and the public posts behind it. Every chart fact names its store category and country. Free. Updated daily.

tools.name: get_ideas
tools.description: Consumer product ideas DECA's engine wrote from the demand signals and judged worth testing, best first, each with the apps and posts it rests on and its expected sign-up rate. Ideas another founder is testing are not shown. Pass id to read one idea. Free.

tools.name: get_my_ideas
tools.description: The ideas DECA's engine wrote for your own workspace from what it knows about you (set in the dashboard under Settings → Your radar), each with why it is yours, and the day's public ideas it picked for you. Needs an API key; a key sees only its own workspace. Read only: it never asks the engine to w

tools.name: quote_test
tools.description: The price of testing an idea with ten days of real ads, before anything is paid. You pay only the ad budget, at cost, in USDC on Base; there is no fee. tools.name: start_test
tools.description: Pay for one option of a quote and open the test. The price is the option's ad budget in USDC on Base, paid over x402. Call it first without `payment`: the answer is an x402 payment request for the exact amount. Pay it with an x402 client and call again with the payment as `payment` (the base64 PAYME

tools.name: get_test
tools.description: A paid test's state and everything in it: payment, review, the pass line, progress and the result. Readable with the key it was paid with, or its access_token.

tools.name: list_my_tests
tools.description: Every test paid with this API key's workspace, newest first. Needs a key.

tools.name: cancel_test
tools.description: Cancel a test that is still in review, before its ads run. The whole budget is refunded to the paying wallet.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_test" references sensitive artifacts (access_token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
